solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cate composed in defeat gives a wave

indicators.note: in says the reworked name sits inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to whip is to defeat soundly

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of Cate are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress named Cate stays calm after losing and waves goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like it describes Cate's calm, but it is the anagram signal; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitecap is a breaking ocean crest topped with white foam, a kind of wave.

clue.text: An instrument of oppression primarily employed by corrupt chairman

indicators.note: employed by says the single letter is taken in by the rearranged word
corrupt means spoilt or twisted, so the letters of chairman are scrambled
primarily means first, so the initial letter of oppression

explanation.surface: A crooked chairman uses a tool of oppression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument of oppression' suggests a weapon or law; the definition is only 'An instrument'. CHAIRMAN rearranged takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, a small musical instrument blown through reeds.

clue.text: Essential to refute Netanyahu's dogma

indicators.note: Essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It is vital to rebut the Israeli leader's doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, much like a dogma.

clue.text: Not entirely reasonable to interrupt Joy's gallant

indicators.note: to interrupt says the shortened word breaks into the middle of the word for joy

parts.note: cheer means joy; the 's is the possessive of the surface

indicators.note: Not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a valid argument is a reasonable one

explanation.surface: A dashing man's behaviour is not quite reasonable enough to spoil Joy's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts the final letter from the word for reasonable, and 'to interrupt' puts what is left inside the word for joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a knight or a chivalrous gentleman, a gallant in the old sense.

clue.text: Reportedly chose to accept socialist's forecast

indicators.note: to accept says the first piece takes the socialist inside it
Reportedly means as it is spoken, so a word that sounds like the synonym for chose

parts.note: picked means chose; said out loud it matches Pict, a member of an ancient people of Scotland
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: It is said someone opted to welcome a socialist's prediction.
explanation.walkthrough: PICT (sounds like picked) holds RED: P-RED-ICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict something is to foretell it, a synonym of the verb forecast.

clue.text: Penny tucked into exceptionally good meal

indicators.note: tucked into says the coin's letter is pushed inside the word for exceptionally good

parts.note: super means exceptionally good
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Someone spends a penny on a really good meal and eats it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' sounds like eating, but here it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, the last eating occasion of the day.

clue.text: Class set about Pinter's first play

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the word for class surrounds the initial

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind

indicators.note: first means the initial letter of Pinter

explanation.surface: A class of students begin work on Harold Pinter's first drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter was a playwright, so 'play' looks theatrical; here it means fun and games.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport is play or amusement, as in doing something in sport.

clue.text: Common fellow found in bar

indicators.note: found in says the man's name sits inside the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to prevent
Al is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap is discovered in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is the verb meaning stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread, frequently found, and so common.

clue.text: Throws out section on English university

indicators.note: on here says the section's letter is put next to the others, at the end

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Discards a section on English from a university course.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' usually puts a piece above another; here S comes last, so 'on' is read as 'added to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or discharge, so emits matches throws out.

clue.text: Country girl without a hint of sophistication

indicators.note: without says the letter that follows is dropped from the girl's name

parts.note: Frances is a girl's name

indicators.note: a hint of means just the first letter of sophistication

explanation.surface: A rustic young woman lacks any trace of worldly polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation of western Europe, an example of a country.

clue.text: Mysterious man clutching note found by well

indicators.note: clutching says the man's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Eric is a man's name

indicators.note: found by says the note sits right beside the word for well

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what now?', can stand for well
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A puzzling fellow holding a note is discovered beside a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' here is the filler word used to start a sentence, not a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select few, hence obscure or mysterious to others.

clue.text: Deny girl's entering a formal agreement

indicators.note: entering says the girl's name goes inside the word for agreement

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement
Di is a girl's name; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A young woman signing a formal contract refuses to admit something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' is the container signal; the 's of girl's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict someone is to deny the truth of what they say.

clue.text: Discovered in collapsed part of church

indicators.note: Discovered in says the answer is found sitting among the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Something found inside a fallen-down section of a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like it might strip outer letters, but with 'in' it simply means found inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually holding the altar.

clue.text: Artist receives one at Welsh festival

indicators.note: receives says the painter's name takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter is welcomed at a celebration in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh festival' reads like an eisteddfod, but 'Welsh' only gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights held each autumn.

clue.text: Right of access for lawyer overturned by embassy

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the lawyer's letters backwards

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer
a mission is a diplomatic embassy

explanation.surface: A lawyer's ruling on entry rights is overruled by an embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is permission to enter, the right to go into a place.

clue.text: Reluctant to pursue right back's cross

indicators.note: to pursue says the word for reluctant follows behind the other piece
back's means right is turned round, the 's acting as is

parts.note: averse means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: A football right-back is unwilling to chase the ball and send in a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right back' looks like a football position, but 'back' is the reversal signal and 'to pursue' puts the word for reluctant second.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross something, travelling from one side to the other.

clue.text: Left after artist turned up needing money for port

indicators.note: after says the letter for left comes behind the other pieces
turned up means the artist's letters are read upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
change is money, especially coins

explanation.surface: Someone left once a painter arrived short of cash for a drink of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine, but it is a harbour town; 'turned up' looks like 'arrived'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel, Arkhangelsk in Russian, is a major port on the White Sea in northern Russia.

clue.text: One with an interest in drawing may choose to do it

definitions.text: One with an interest in drawing may choose to do it

parts.words: One with an interest in drawing may choose to do it
parts.note: drawing suggests an artist, but in cricket a batsman wanting a draw blocks every ball defensively

explanation.surface: Someone keen on sketching might decide to try this.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a drawn match is neither won nor lost; a side settling for a draw bats ultra-defensively to avoid getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to bat or act obstructively and defensively, blocking progress to avoid losing.

clue.text: Soldiers introduced to mother during dance in Scottish castle

indicators.note: during says the mother group sits in the middle of the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: introduced to says the soldiers go inside the word for mother

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops meet someone's mother at a dance held in a castle in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' and 'during' are both container signals, one nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Merciful earl nurses injured linnet? Just the opposite

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, a containment signal
Just the opposite says the roles swap, so the jumbled bird holds the nobleman instead
injured means damaged, so the letters of linnet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kindly nobleman cares for a hurt songbird, or rather the bird cares for him.
explanation.walkthrough: LINNET rearranged holds E, giving LEN-E-IENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient person is mild and tolerant, showing mercy rather than severity.

clue.text: Against including over the top material

indicators.note: including says the word for against wraps around the other abbreviation

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a fabric that is too extravagant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is a soft fabric woven from the fibre of the cotton plant.

clue.text: Chooses to behead old Egyptians

indicators.note: to behead means the first letter is cut off the word

parts.note: the Copts are Egyptian Christians, descendants of the ancient Egyptians

explanation.surface: Someone decides to decapitate ancient Egyptians.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt for something is to choose it, so opts is a synonym of picks.

clue.text: Prized example of a decorative border by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is spoken, giving one that is spelt differently

parts.note: purl is an ornamental edging of looped thread on lace or embroidery

explanation.surface: A treasured sample of an ornamental edge, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the finest of its kind is called a pearl, as in a pearl among cities.

clue.text: Details released after Brown is teased

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come behind the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: released means set free, so the letters of Details are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Once the particulars are made public, a man called Brown is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname, but it is the colour; 'released' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to tease by offering something then keeping it out of reach.

clue.text: Discover vehicle upside-down at end of lane

indicators.note: upside-down in a down clue means the vehicle's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of lane

explanation.surface: Finding an overturned vehicle at the far end of a country road.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it down and find it.

clue.text: Small bay mare's tail is wrapped in lint after surgery

indicators.note: wrapped in says the horse's last letter is bound up inside the scrambled dressing
after surgery means operated on, so the letters of lint are rearranged
tail means the last letter of mare

explanation.surface: After an operation, a bay horse's tail is bandaged in lint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a horse's colour beside 'mare', but 'Small bay' is the definition. LINT rearranged wraps E: IN-E-LT reordered to INL-E-T.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea reaching into the land, a small bay or creek.

clue.text: Gained converts with graduate's witty conversation

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate; the 's means has

indicators.note: converts means changes form, so the letters of Gained are rearranged

explanation.surface: A graduate wins over new followers through clever talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for followers, but it is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, joking banter between people.

clue.text: City finding goalscorer's head almost every time

indicators.note: head means the first letter of goalscorer
almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: always means every time

explanation.surface: A city where the leading striker scores nearly every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is a city on the west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Catch a glimpse of German weapon

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by knights

explanation.surface: Someone briefly spots a German weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance at something is to look at it quickly, getting only a brief view.

clue.text: Count on story being revealing

parts.note: to tell is to count, as a bank teller counts money
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Rely on a story to reveal something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' looks like 'rely on', but 'on' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign gives something away, revealing what was meant to be hidden.
